title: H1 2026 Topicus.com Inc. update ($TOI)
content_html:
Dear partners,

Earlier this year, I wrote an investment thesis on Topicus. Yesterday evening, the serial acquirer in VMS businesses released its Q2 figures. Since quarterly figures say little about the long term, I will monitor whether anything fundamentally changes. I will briefly give you the investment summary I wrote earlier this year.

Investment Thesis (Summary)

Topicus.com Inc. (TOI) represents a rare opportunity to invest in a European compounding machine that is benefiting from the structural consolidation of the fragmented Vertical Market Software (VMS) sector. While the broader software market is currently grappling with uncertainty (Topicus 60% lower than it’s 52-week high of $199 CAD) due to the rise of Artificial Intelligence. This is an opportunity for the long-term contrarian investor.

At current price levels, Topicus is trading below its intrinsic value. My analysis indicates that the market overestimates the risk of AI disruption for niche VMS, while Topicus actually benefits from high barriers to entry due to limited public data and a small market size, which distinguishes it from vulnerable Horizontal Market Software (HMS). With a conservative ‘exit multiple’ of 15x in the base case scenario, the current valuation offers a significant margin of safety. My thesis rests on three central pillars:

  1. Fundamental AI Resilience: The deep integration of VMS in regulated sectors (data & privacy) acts as a defensive shield. While HMS is being disrupted by public data models, Topicus’s closed, niche-specific critical data for its costumers remains with pricing power and sticky recurring revenue.

  2. Cash Generation & Capital Discipline: With negative Net Working Capital and strong unlevered Free Cash Flow (uFCF) enables Topicus to finance its expansion almost entirely autonomously. With a Net Debt/EBITDA ratio of just 1.1x, the company has a solid balance sheet with the optional flexibility to accelerate growth through strategic leverage.

  3. Proven ROIIC Flywheel: As a master of the “build and buy” strategy within the Constellation ecosystem, Topicus consistently converts capital into a superior return on invested capital (& ROIIC). The runway of an estimated 200,000 potential targets worldwide guarantees a long-term growth trajectory.

H1 and Q2 2026 Results

Topicus's business units mostly sell software licenses and maintenance contracts through a subscription model (SaaS). Revenue has grown at a CAGR of ~25% since 2018, fed by mergers and acquisitions (M&A) and organic growth of the units. That engine kept running in Q2. Revenue rose 18% YoY to €437.3 million. For the first half, revenue grew 20% to €872.9 million:

Total expenses (excluding amortization) rose 18% to €333.8 million. This quarter the operating leverage paused, expenses held at 76% of revenue, flat versus Q2 2025. For the half year, however, expenses fell to 75% of revenue from 76%, so the six-month picture still shows the cost line growing a touch slower than the top line. .

Topicus’s revenue remains high quality: 72.6% of Q2 revenue is maintenance and other recurring revenue. As a serial acquirer, Topicus keeps buying and building higher-quality revenue, which earns a premium precisely in uncertain times.

Beyond acquiring companies (Buy), Topicus excels at the organic development (Build) of digital ecosystems in education, healthcare and finance. Build is the most profitable route to growth for a serial acquirer. Organic growth cooled slightly this quarter, total organic growth was 4% in Q2 and 5% for the first half. The important engine held firm, though maintenance and other recurring revenue grew 6% organically, which is very positive.

Organic growth shows Topicus can raise prices. That matters, because it proves the software keeps getting more valuable to customers every year even without new acquisitions, especially in these AI-uncertain times.

"We believe shareholder value is created by managing two financial components over the long term: profitability and growth. As such, our corporate bonus plan, which compensates employees at all levels of our organization, is based upon ROIC, net revenue growth and organic revenue growth." — Daan Dijkhuizen, Topicus Annual Report 2021

A note on H1 headline profit

At first glance, half-year net income fell 8% to €102.4 million. The prior-year comparison is flattered by a one-off €32.8 million fair-value gain that Topicus booked on its Asseco stake in H1 2025. Strip that non-operating noise out and the underlying business grew. In Q2 itself, net income actually rose 14% to €47.3 million (€0.36 per diluted share versus €0.31).

Asseco

The fair value based on Asseco's share price dropped from €1,038.9 million at year-end to €747.4 million at June 30. The equity method conveniently smooths that volatility off the income statement, carrying the investment at €454.7 million. We will judge the Asseco deal on cash returns and eventual influence, not on accounting that hides the mark-to-market. As the value of Asseco will fluctuate:

Operating cash flows

Here the calendar flips. In Q1, Topicus collects a disproportionate share of annual maintenance billings, so the cash floods in. Q2 operating cash flow was negative €12.7 million. This is normal seasonality. For the first six months, operating cash flow still grew 4% to €267.8 million.

Free cash flow available to shareholders (FCFA2S) for the half year rose 24% to €180.1 million. A large chunk of that jump is a €59.0 million dividend received from Asseco in Q2.

In Q1 managemant used the cash flows to reduce the variable debt on the revolving credit facility. The drawn balance on the Topicus Revolving Credit Facility fell from €335.0 million at year-end to €110.0 million at June 30. With a €700 million facility now largely undrawn, Topicus has roughly €590 million of dry powder ready for acquisitions. Exactly the position we want a disciplined acquirer to be in.

Buy & Build strategy

Topicus's engine is the disciplined "Buy & Build" playbook that grew Total Specific Solutions from a handful of units to a decentralized federation of independent businesses. This quarter, the pace of deployment stayed deliberately slow. Total consideration for acquisitions in the first half was just €62.7 million (€46.3 million cash plus €10.9 million holdbacks and €5.6 million contingent consideration). Compare that to €258.9 million of cash deployed on acquisitions in the same period last year.

Over the last year we have watched public software valuations fall 50–60% or more. That makes listed companies interesting acquisition targets. For example, the Asseco move. Private markets, however, have not repriced nearly as much. As Mark Miller (CSI) put it last quarter:

“Nothing’s really changed. We’re looking at both private companies and public companies, both for acquisition and for PEMS. We haven’t really seen on the private side any change in pricing so far, and competition for those businesses is still very strong… There’s just been a little bit of change in pricing for publicly traded companies.” - Mark Miller, CEO CSI

Olle Backman (Vitec) framed the buyer’s side of the same standoff:

“The expectations from our side has certainly de-rated… The private markets are moving really slow, and there’s not a lot of deals that has been done.” - Olle Backman, CEO Vitec Software Group

Through last quarter, sellers in private M&A were still anchored to high prices, so disciplined buyers waited. But the picture may finally be starting to shift. Neil Hunn, CEO of Roper Technologies and one of the most disciplined capital allocators in VMS, offered a fresher read on July 23, 2026:

“We expect the private (VMS) values to mirror those or come down to the public values. We’re starting to see some very early signs of that. As we all know, public values are ultimately the gravitational force for all private companies.” - Neil Hunn, CEO Roper Technologies, July 23, 2026

This is exactly the development we have been hoping for. Public multiples have already collapsed. If Hunn is right that private values are now being pulled down by that same gravity, it is good news for a buyer with a loaded balance sheet, these very early signs harden into a real repricing.

And Topicus is positioned. Subsequent to June 30, it completed or committed to acquisitions worth €56.1 million (€43.4 million cash on closing plus €12.7 million in deferred payments), across the fleet, healthcare and education verticals. So the optional cash pile is not sitting idle out of indecision, most importantly management is deploying, just at hurdle rates it can defend (Hopefully).

Conclusion Casteleyn Partnership

A solid quarter, which is exactly what long-term owners should want. We would like nothing more than for the private M&A market to finally cool, so Topicus can strike harder. Until then, we are content to acquire more Topicus shares when prices are destressed and let a disciplined management do what it does best.

As Charlie Munger reminded us: “The big money is not in the buying and the selling, but in the waiting.”

Patient capital. Driven by the discipline of learning. — Casteleyn Partnership
